Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery call and a proposed set of next steps so we can qualify the Dedicated capacity setup for Acme: 

What we covered (summary)

- Primary use cases: realtime chat completions + nightly reranking/embeddings refresh jobs.
- Security: customer-managed keys (KMS) + VPC-only control plane required.
- Success criteria: sub-200ms 95th for small-completion paths, predictable throughput for batched reranks.

Integration/architecture items we need to confirm

2) Routing: route high-QPS, latency-sensitive traffic to a low-latency pool; route nightly batch rerank to a lower-priority pool with higher batching to save cost.
3) Structured output/tool-calling: you plan to use function/tool calling for extraction and a structured JSON schema for downstream processing — we’ll provide the model wiring guide.
4) Embeddings & rerankers: embeddings workload will be on a dedicated pool with async batching and a KV cache for hot vectors.
5) Autoscaling/throughput sizing: we need concrete concurrency/latency targets per model to size the pool and policy. See proposed checklist below.

Checklist / next steps

- Tom: share current SLA/latency targets per route.
- Marissa/Aditya: provide sample SDK config, mTLS guidelines, and a reference autoscale policy by EOD tomorrow. (Aditya looping in for sizing)
- Meet: 30-min technical deep-dive next week to finalize autoscale thresholds and queue strategy.

Hi Tom — looping in with technical details and a proposed autoscale policy. Thanks for the qps CSV — that’s very helpful. Answers inline: 

1) Queue vs reject/backpressure
- Recommendation: queue-first with backpressure thresholds. Use a short in-memory request queue in the ingress (per-pool) and configure two thresholds: soft queue depth (start shedding non-critical batch jobs to lower-priority pool) and hard queue depth (return 429 when full). This gives you graceful degradation for realtime requests while protecting the serving runtime.

2) Avoiding hallucinations for structured output/tool-calling
- Use strongly-typed function schemas and response validators on the client-side. Combine token-level constraints (stop sequences, temperature) with model-level fine-tuning/format-instruction prompts. For critical extractions, run a fast deterministic verifier step (small classifier or schema validator) and retry with a clarifying prompt if validation fails.

Proposed sample autoscale policy (attached):
- Target concurrency per-GPU: 40 concurrent small-completion sessions (avg seq len 64)
- Pool min-size: 4 GPUs; max-size: 32 GPUs
- Scale-up trigger: average queue depth > 20 for 30s OR 95th latency > 220ms for 60s
- Scale-down trigger: average queue depth = 0 and 95th latency < 180ms for 5m
- Priority routing: realtime pool > batch pool; batch pool has larger batch windows and higher throughput per-GPU.

SDK/mTLS notes:
- We’ll provide an SDK sample that supports both API-key and mTLS handshakes. For your VPC/Dedicated deployment, enable mTLS at the ingress and use short-lived certs synchronized via your internal PKI.

Attachments included: sample-autoscale-policy.yaml (contains the YAML policy and suggested concurrency numbers) and a one-page reference for mTLS setup.

Happy to walk through the YAML in the technical deep-dive — propose Wed 10am PT.
